title: Enforce deploy gating when tier error budget is exhausted (non-emergency deploys)
creator: Aisha Bello
description:
Move deploy gating from warn-only (ENG-4935) to enforced blocking for non-emergency deploys when a tier is in a red error-budget state (exhausted budget or actively burning at high rate, per policy).

Scope
- Gate applies to: control plane, routing/policy evaluator, API gateway, serving request-path services (incl. streaming handlers), and shared libraries that materially affect request path behavior.
- Enforce for: non-critical deploys into production environments (hosted + dedicated tiers). Staging remains warn-only.
- Exemptions: emergency fixes with explicit override pathway and logging.

Goal
- Reduce compounding reliability regressions during active budget burn and align with the error budget policy consequences (release freeze when exhausted).

Non-goals
- Private tier enforcement (future phase).
- Blocking config-only changes for mitigations (these should remain allowed if they improve reliability).
acceptance_criteria:
- When budget state is RED (exhausted) for a tier, CI/CD blocks production deploys that match the gated service list unless an emergency override is used.
- When burn-rate alert is firing at SEV-2+ (per ENG-4930), CI/CD blocks production deploys for impacted tier(s) unless emergency override is used.
- Emergency override requires: Jira/Linear incident reference or on-call approval acknowledgement, reason text, and is posted to #eng-sre and #eng-platform with deploy link.
- Every override is logged with: actor, timestamp, service, environment, tier(s) affected, budget state snapshot, and justification.
- Rollbacks are always allowed (even in RED), including reverting the immediately previous version.
- A "mitigation allowlist" exists for safe operational changes (e.g., routing policy adjustments, capacity knobs) that SRE can apply during incidents without being blocked.
- Clear developer-facing error message from gate includes: which tier is RED, links to dashboard/runbook, and how to request an override.
- Dry-run / audit mode available per environment flag; can be toggled off only by SRE on-call or release gate owner.
- Documentation updated with the emergency pathway and examples; CS/SE can reference what the gate means operationally (not customer-facing SLO language).
implementation_notes:
Current baseline
- Warn-only gate merged in PR-28510: emits warnings, Slack notification, and records a "gate would have blocked" audit event.
- Error budget state source: budget computation job output (rolling window) + burn-rate alert state (Prometheus/Alertmanager).

Proposed enforcement behavior
1) Decision inputs
- Budget state: GREEN / YELLOW / RED (from budget pipeline)
- Active burn: burn-rate alert firing (multi-window) with severity mapping
- Tier targeting: Hosted vs Dedicated tags; if service deploy is tier-agnostic, default to "block if either tier is RED".

2) Gate logic
- Block if (budget_state == RED) OR (burn_alert_firing == true AND severity >= SEV-2)
- Allow if deploy is tagged as rollback OR mitigation-allowlisted OR emergency override present.

3) Emergency pathway
- Require an override token generated by incident-bot OR a manually entered "override reason" that includes:
  - Incident key (INC-####) OR Linear issue key (ENG-####) for mitigation work
  - Approver: "SRE on-call" (name) for non-rollback deploys
- Post to Slack with a structured message (service, sha, env, tier, reason, approver).

4) Guardrails
- Enforce a max override TTL (e.g., 2 hours) to prevent stale override reuse.
- Rate limit overrides per service to avoid override spam.
- Emit metrics: deploy_gate_blocks_total, deploy_gate_overrides_total, deploy_gate_rollbacks_total labeled by service/env/tier/reason.

Open questions
- Whether config-only changes in routing/policy should always bypass the gate or be included in mitigation allowlist only.
- How to handle shared libraries used by both request-path and non-request-path services (recommend: gate only services, not libs).
rollout_plan:
Phase 0 (complete): Warn-only in prod (PR-28510). Collect data on false positives/false negatives.
Phase 1 (this ticket): Enforced blocking in prod for a small gated service subset (gateway + routing) for 1 week; others remain warn-only.
Phase 2: Expand to serving request-path services once we validate rollback allowances + override flow.
Phase 3: Turn on "block if either tier RED" for shared services; confirm Dedicated-only services gate only on Dedicated.

Operational readiness
- Update on-call playbook: what to do when a deploy is blocked during an incident.
- Confirm incident-bot message includes links: tiered SLO dashboard, burn-rate panel, mitigation runbook.

Success metrics
- During SEV-2+ incidents, number of non-emergency deploys drops to near zero.
- No net increase in MTTR due to gate (rollbacks remain unblocked; mitigations allowed).
- Less budget overspend from compounding changes during active burn windows.
risk_and_mitigations:
Risk: Gate blocks needed mitigations.
- Mitigation: mitigation allowlist owned by SRE; rollbacks always allowed; emergency override path.

Risk: False RED due to telemetry gaps or tier-tagging bugs.
- Mitigation: gate checks data quality flag from budget pipeline; if data quality is degraded, fall back to warn-only and page Telemetry.

Risk: Engineers bypass via emergency override too often.
- Mitigation: override audit review weekly; alert on high override rate; require SRE on-call approver for non-rollback.

Risk: Confusion about tier impact.
- Mitigation: gate message explicitly states which tier(s) are in RED and links to the correct dashboard filter.

comments: 2026-01-29 — Aisha Bello: Creating follow-on to ENG-4935. We have enough warn-only data now; during 01/18 regression we still shipped a routing tweak mid-burn. Need hard stop for non-emergency prod deploys.
2026-01-31 — Connor O'Brien: +1 on rollbacks always allowed. Also recommend gating by service category list (request-path) rather than repo to avoid accidentally blocking tooling deploys.

2026-02-03 — Sahana Iyer: Drafted gate decision tree: (RED budget OR SEV2 burn alert) => block unless rollback/mitigation/override. Working on override TTL + Slack payload format. Will share with SRE for review.

2026-02-05 — Rafael Mendes: Please ensure we can still push routing policy mitigations during incidents without needing an override every time. Suggest explicit mitigation allowlist owned by SRE on-call with an audited change record.

2026-02-07 — Jordan Lee: One nuance: tier-agnostic shared services should block if either tier is RED; dedicated-only services should only consider Dedicated budget. Can we wire tier impact from deploy metadata? If not, we’ll need a static mapping table.

2026-02-10 — Sahana Iyer: Implemented mapping table in gate config (service -> impacted_tiers). Defaults to both tiers if unknown. Added data-quality check from budget pipeline; if stale/missing > 30m, gate falls back to warn-only and opens a Telemetry page.

2026-02-13 — Sean Gallagher: Reviewed PR-28541. Looks good. Ask: add explicit copy in the failure message about emergency path + include who to page (SRE on-call). Also ensure the override logs land in the same index as incident audits.

2026-02-16 — Sahana Iyer: Addressed review notes: improved gate messaging, added structured audit log fields, and wired Slack notification to #eng-sre + #release-eng. Ready for final approval; proposing Phase 1 rollout (gateway + routing only) starting 02/18.
